segments.contextAfter: The main overall change is a vertically stacked, mostly single-column layout that typically produces narrower alert panels or sheets than in previous OS releases. This change in alert width affects line wrap of [`messageText`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/AppKit/NSAlert/messageText) and [`informativeText`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/AppKit/NSAlert/informativeText) content. Apps that use hard line breaks in their alert text or count on line wrap occurring at particular places in previous releases may need to reformat their alert content for macOS Big Sur 11 beta. Uses of [`accessoryView`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/AppKit/NSAlert/accessoryView) with NSAlerts may likewise need revising to work well with `NSAlert`s’ new layout and appearance. Controls presented in an alert’s `accessoryView` should use the new .large control size on macOS Big Sur 11 beta. You may also reconsider the width of each `accessoryView` you’re using. An alert will widen itself when feasible to accommodate a given `accessoryView`‘s width (in previous releases, an `NSAlert` attempts to maintain the frame size of the `accessoryView`), but the resultant alert’s proportions might not fit optimally with the system look, if the `accessoryView` is very wide. In such cases, you may want to reduce the accessoryView’s width if that can be done without negatively impacting user interaction with the `accessoryView`’s controls.

Handle the first responder behavior based on the way macOS presents search results. The first type is the filtering search. The results are presented by filtering non-matching items from a list. The second type is the query search. macOS presents the results by showing a designated view. Finder and Calendar are of this type. The search remains focused, with the cancel button allowing continued search sessions. The query type search apps changes `resignsFirstResponderWithCancel` to `false`.
